disclaimer: stellar-guard reports potential issues found by source-level heuristics. Findings are not proof of a vulnerability, and a clean scan does not prove a contract is secure.

findings.message: This contract writes persistent storage but never extends its TTL; entries will be archived when their TTL expires
findings.help: Extend the TTL where entries are written or read, e.g. `env.storage().persistent().extend_ttl(&key, THRESHOLD, EXTEND_TO)` and `env.storage().instance().extend_ttl(THRESHOLD, EXTEND_TO)` in frequently called functions.

findings.message: Exported function `withdraw` transfers tokens out of the contract without an authorization check
findings.help: Review whether this operation requires `address.require_auth()` (on the affected user or the stored admin). If the function is intentionally permissionless, add `// stellar-guard-ignore SG-001 -- <reason>`.

findings.message: Exported function `set_admin` modifies privileged configuration without an authorization check
findings.help: Review whether this operation requires `address.require_auth()` (on the affected user or the stored admin). If the function is intentionally permissionless, add `// stellar-guard-ignore SG-001 -- <reason>`.

findings.message: This contract writes instance storage but never extends its TTL; entries will be archived when their TTL expires
findings.help: Extend the TTL where entries are written or read, e.g. `env.storage().persistent().extend_ttl(&key, THRESHOLD, EXTEND_TO)` and `env.storage().instance().extend_ttl(THRESHOLD, EXTEND_TO)` in frequently called functions.

findings.message: Exported function `set_admin` modifies privileged configuration without publishing a Soroban event
findings.help: Publish an event with `env.events().publish(..)` so off-chain consumers can monitor this change.

findings.help: Add `if amount <= 0 { panic_with_error!(..) }` (or `< 0` if zero is allowed) before using it.

findings.message: Exported function `move_balance` decreases a value keyed by `from`, but only `caller` authorizes
findings.help: Call `from.require_auth()` before debiting it, or check an allowance granted by `from` to the caller.
findings.snippet: write_balance(&env, &from, balance - amount); // expect: SG-001, SG-006

findings.message: Exported function `withdraw_signed` calls `require_auth_for_args` without `to`, `amount` in the signed arguments
findings.help: Include every amount and address that the call acts on in the `require_auth_for_args` arguments, or use `require_auth()` so the full invocation is signed.

rules.name: missing-authorization
rules.description: An exported contract function writes to storage, transfers tokens out of the contract, or upgrades the contract WASM, but neither it nor any helper it calls invokes `require_auth()` / `require_auth_for_args()` (or a recognised access-control helper or attribute). Anyone can call such a function with arbitrary arguments.
rules.remediation: Review whether this operation requires `address.require_auth()` (on the affected user or the stored admin). If the function is intentionally permissionless, add `// stellar-guard-ignore SG-001 -- <reason>`.

rules.name: storage-tier-misuse
rules.summary: Suspicious storage type for application state
rules.description: Soroban has three storage tiers. Temporary entries are permanently deleted when their TTL expires and cannot be restored, so storing balances, admin addresses, configuration or other long-lived state there can silently lose funds or brick the contract. Instance storage is loaded on every invocation and shares one size-limited ledger entry, so writing per-user keys (e.g. `DataKey::Balance(addr)`) to it grows the entry without bound and raises costs for every caller.
rules.remediation: Keep long-lived state in `persistent()` (per-user data) or `instance()` (small contract-wide config) and extend its TTL; reserve `temporary()` for data that may safely disappear.

rules.name: unchecked-arithmetic
rules.description: Plain `+`, `-`, `*` (and their assignment forms) on values that look like token amounts or balances, and `as` casts of such values to a narrower integer type. In release builds without `overflow-checks = true`, integer overflow wraps silently, which can mint balances or bypass limits. `as` casts never check: `amount as u64` truncates and `amount as u128` turns negative amounts into huge positive ones.
rules.remediation: Use `checked_add` / `checked_sub` / `checked_mul` and handle `None`, set `overflow-checks = true` in `[profile.release]`, and replace `as` casts with `try_from`.

rules.name: unbounded-iteration
rules.description: A loop or iterator chain walks a collection that is loaded from contract storage, or a collection / count supplied by the caller, without an upper bound check. Soroban transactions have hard CPU, memory and ledger-read limits. If a stored collection can grow without limit (for example, anyone can append to a list of users), the function will eventually exceed those limits and become permanently uncallable, which can lock funds. Caller-supplied sizes let a single caller force expensive work.
rules.remediation: Check `len()` (or the count) against a maximum before looping, paginate with `start`/`limit` arguments, or store each entry under its own key instead of one growing `Vec`/`Map`.

rules.name: unprotected-initializer
rules.summary: Initializer can be called more than once
rules.description: An exported function named like an initializer (`initialize`, `init`, …) writes contract state but never checks whether the contract has already been initialized. Because exported functions are callable by anyone, an attacker can call it again after deployment to replace the admin, token address or other configuration, or front-run the legitimate first call.
rules.remediation: Move initialization into `__constructor` (runs once at deployment), or fail when already initialized, e.g. `if env.storage().instance().has(&DataKey::Admin) { panic_with_error!(..) }`.

rules.name: negative-amount
rules.summary: Signed amount not checked for negative values
rules.description: Soroban token amounts are `i128`, so they can be negative. An exported function that writes an `i128` parameter into contract storage (balances, shares, debts, limits), directly or through helpers, without checking its sign lets a caller invert the operation: a negative mint burns, a negative deposit credits less than zero, a negative debt repayment borrows. Amounts that are also passed to an external token call are not reported, because token contracts reject negative amounts and the whole invocation fails.
rules.remediation: Reject negative (and usually zero) amounts before using them, e.g. `if amount <= 0 { panic_with_error!(&env, Error::InvalidAmount) }`, or use an unsigned type.

rules.name: missing-ttl-extension
rules.summary: Stored data never has its TTL extended
rules.description: Persistent and instance entries live only until their time-to-live (TTL) runs out; they are then archived and every call that reads them fails until someone restores them. A contract that writes persistent or instance storage but never calls `extend_ttl` on that tier (and never extends its instance with the deployer) relies on users or operators to extend or restore entries by hand. Archived instance storage makes the whole contract unusable until restored. Writes made only by `__constructor` or an initializer are not considered.
rules.remediation: Extend the TTL where entries are written or read, e.g. `env.storage().persistent().extend_ttl(&key, THRESHOLD, EXTEND_TO)` and `env.storage().instance().extend_ttl(THRESHOLD, EXTEND_TO)` in frequently called functions.

rules.name: ignored-try-call
rules.summary: Result of a fallible cross-contract call is ignored
rules.description: Generated contract clients offer `try_*` variants (`client.try_transfer(..)`) that return a `Result` instead of aborting when the callee fails. Dropping that result (`client.try_transfer(..);` or `let _ = client.try_transfer(..);`) lets execution continue as if the call succeeded: tokens were not moved, a hook did not run, state was not updated, yet the caller records success.
rules.remediation: Use the non-`try_` method so a failure aborts the invocation, or handle the `Result` explicitly (`match client.try_transfer(..) { Ok(Ok(())) => .., _ => panic_with_error!(..) }`).

rules.name: weak-check-auth
rules.summary: Custom account `__check_auth` does not verify the signature
rules.description: A custom account contract authorizes every action taken on its behalf through `__check_auth(env, signature_payload, signatures, auth_contexts)`. If the implementation never uses the payload or the signatures, or never calls a signature-verification function (`ed25519_verify`, `secp256r1_verify`, `secp256k1_recover`, `bls12_381` checks) or delegates to another account's `require_auth`, then any transaction can spend the account's funds.
rules.remediation: Verify every signature against `signature_payload` (e.g. `env.crypto().ed25519_verify(&public_key, &signature_payload.into(), &signature)`) and check that the signer is authorized for each entry of `auth_contexts`.

rules.name: missing-admin-events
rules.summary: Privileged changes do not publish an event
rules.description: An exported contract function upgrades the contract or writes a privileged storage key without publishing a Soroban event itself or through a helper it calls. Events make these changes easier for indexers and operators to monitor off-chain.
rules.remediation: Publish a descriptive event with `env.events().publish(..)` when the privileged change occurs, directly or through a helper.
